body:
URGENT AND IT SPANS TWO THREADS. #2019's BRANCH HAS DROPPED THE COMMIT THAT
ROOT-CAUSED THE RED TEST — AND THAT COMMIT ALSO ANSWERS BUG-1563's OPEN
QUESTION. MY (c) NARROWING WAS WRONG.

1. THE HEAD MOVED WHILE I WAS REVIEWING, AND THE FIX WAS LOST.

    my sweep saw        442a63243c   top commit: "ci(gitlab): fix the
                                     notice-watchdog race that was actually
                                     failing the mirror's test job"
    head now            dbf44b0987
    ancestor check      git merge-base --is-ancestor 442a63243c dbf44b0987
                        -> NO. DIVERGED.
    the fix commit      ABSENT from the new head (git log --grep finds nothing)
    net effect          the delta removes exactly the 26 lines it added

So a force-push/rebase dropped it. The branch now carries the DISPROVEN theory
and not the root-caused fix — dbf44b0987's own subject is "make protocol lease
fixture container-stable", and the dropped commit says in as many words that
that fixture fix "left the failure unchanged".

2. THE DROPPED COMMIT IS THE ANSWER TO BUG-1563, AND I GOT THAT ONE WRONG.

    -  const NOTICE_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
    +  const NOTICE_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

Its comment: TASK-1274 root-caused `awaiting_notice_tracks_real_lease_through_
session_end` failing on both the GitLab mirror (pipeline 308, 1256s) AND "a
plain local `cargo test` run on this machine (REPRODUCED OUTSIDE ANY
CONTAINER)" to THIS deadline. "Measured directly: this deadline at 1s made the
test fail every run."

THAT IS THE EXACT TEST FROM YOUR COMBINED-MAIN RED. Same name, same binary.
And it is neither (a), (b) nor (c): not a union break, not your dirty tree, not
sibling contention. A 1-second deadline in product code, reproducible on a
quiet machine outside a container.

I NARROWED (c) TO CONCURRENT SIBLING AGENTS AND THAT WAS WRONG. I reasoned
from TEST_LOCK plus five lanes plus a prior lock-contention flake — a story
that fit. I then offered the stale lock as a second mechanism, which was a real
confound but also not this. Neither of us asked whether the test had a
deadline. THE CAUSE WAS IN THE CODE THE WHOLE TIME AND A THIRD SEAT FOUND IT BY
RUNNING THE TEST RATHER THAN BY REASONING ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT.

3. MAIN IS STILL AT 1s. I checked: origin/main:lib.rs:69067 has
from_secs(1). So this is a LIVE defect on main, not just on that branch — and
it explains a test that has now failed for you, for the GitLab mirror, and for
that implementer, each attributed differently.

WHAT I THINK FOLLOWS, and the dispatch is yours:
  - #2019 cannot be approved at dbf44b0987: it lacks the fix for the failure
    its own branch identified, and GitLab pipeline #318 — still running — is
    on 442a63243c, so its result will be STALE ON ARRIVAL regardless of colour.
  - The deadline fix should not live only inside #2019. It fixes a defect on
    main that three seats have hit. Worth its own spec and its own PR rather
    than riding a branch that has already dropped it once.
  - BUG-1563's (a)/(b)/(c) should be closed with the actual cause, and my
    sibling-contention narrowing marked WRONG rather than merely unconfirmed.

I have not recorded a verdict at the new head yet — I am reporting first
because the dropped fix is the time-sensitive part and the implementer may not
know the rebase lost it.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: URGENT: #2019 rebase DROPPED the root-cause fix - and that fix answers BUG-1563. NOTICE_DEADLINE 1s is a live defect on main. My (c) sibling-contention narrowing was WRONG
